items.title: AJK assembly adopts resolutions condemning ministers’ remarks, backing the Truth and Reconciliation Commission
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Legislative Assembly on Thursday unanimously adopted two resolutions on the recent unrest in Rawalakot and other parts of the region, with one condemning statements by federal ministers on the crisis and the other endorsing the establishment of an independent Truth and Reconciliation Commission to probe the violence and pave the way for a negotiated settlement. This development emerged amid polls in AJK, which are being held in three phases over security concerns, with the first set of polls held in Mirpur division on Monday. Scuffles, violence and allegations of rigging marred the polling process, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice. The assembly met under the chairmanship of panel member Nabeela Ayoub, but only nine members were in attendance — seven from the ruling PPP and one each from the opposition PML-N and PTI. The first resolution was tabled by former AJK president Sardar Muhammad Yaqoob Khan on Wednesday, while the second was tabled by PPP regional president Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin. Yaqoob, however, was not present during today’s session. Endorsing his resolution, the assembly condemned what it described as “irresponsible” statements by federal ministers regarding the recent Rawalakot incidents. The resolution particularly censured Defence Minister Khawaja Asif for allegedly refusing to recognise the people of Rawalakot as Kashmiris, saying that such remarks had hurt public sentiment and should have been taken notice of by the prime minister. Recalling the role of the people of Poonch in the Pakistan Movement and the state’s subsequent accession to Pakistan, the resolution said that those whose skins had been flayed alive in 1832 belonged to the same land. Continuing, the resolution said that Ghulam Haider Jhandalvi, who had represented the Kashmiris at the adoption of the Pakistan Resolution in Lahore on March 23, 1940, and AJK’s founding president Sardar Muhammad Ibrahim Khan, at whose Srinagar residence the July 19, 1947, accession resolution was adopted, were also sons of the same soil. The resolution said the federal ministers’ statements had “added fuel to the fire” and negatively affected people in Rawalakot, elsewhere in the state and among the Kashmiri diaspora. It called for the implementation of PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari’s proposal to establish a Truth and Reconciliation Commission and urged that no further action be taken in Rawalakot until such a mechanism was put in place. The resolution further called on the Election Commission to ensure free and fair elections and demanded that alleged irregularities in the recent elections in the Mirpur division be addressed before fresh polling. It also stressed that dialogue was the only way forward, warning that continued confrontation would only harm the people of the state while providing India with an opportunity to exploit the situation internationally. It described a Truth and Reconciliation Commission as the only viable means of preventing further instability. The assembly also unanimously adopted the second, much more detailed resolution moved by Yasin, reaffirming its commitment to constitutional supremacy, democracy, the rule of law, and the protection of life and property. The resolution paid tribute to security forces, police and law enforcement personnel who lost their lives in the line of duty and expressed sympathy with the families of all civilians, police personnel and security officials killed or injured during the recent unrest. While affirming that peaceful protest, freedom of expression, and the presentation of legitimate political, economic, administrative and social demands were constitutional and democratic rights, it declared that the use of weapons, violence, vandalism, intimidation and other unlawful means could not be accepted as legitimate means of political struggle. It called on peaceful protesters to distance themselves from armed and violent elements and stressed that responsibility for any offences should be determined individually through evidence, transparent investigations and due legal process. It also demanded that the government and law enforcement agencies act against armed and violent elements without discrimination and in accordance with the Constitution and the law, making clear that the objective of state action should be the enforcement of the law and the restoration of peace rather than revenge. The resolution reiterated that no individual, political party or organisation would be allowed to challenge the writ of the state through force or violence, while insisting that all people arrested and those under investigation must be dealt with in accordance with constitutional guarantees, fair trial requirements and judicial procedures. It also expressed sorrow over the loss of life and property suffered by citizens during the recent tensions and called for all such incidents to be examined through an impartial, transparent and lawful process without any predetermined conclusions. In this regard, the assembly supported, in principle, the establishment of an independent, impartial and appropriately empowered Truth and Reconciliation Commission to examine the causes and sequence of the recent crisis, all deaths, injuries, property losses and allegations concerning violence and the use of weapons. The resolution additionally proposed that the federal government and representatives of the protesters jointly endorse in writing the establishment, composition, terms of reference, scope and procedure of the commission, after which the AJK government should constitute it without delay under the relevant law. It further proposed that such an endorsement should be accompanied by an immediate end to protests and simultaneous de-escalation by the government, including the restoration of roads, emergency and medical access, essential supplies, communications, including mobile and internet services, and normal civic and economic activity. It also envisaged that protesting parties would refrain from resuming protests until the commission completed its findings, while the governments of AJK and Pakistan would pause further action pending the inquiry, except where necessary to address specific and imminent threats to life or public safety. The proposed commission would be mandated to examine all relevant records, FIRs, documents, videos, forensic material, communications and testimony, while allowing all affected families and relevant parties to present evidence. It would not determine criminal guilt or impose punishment, but could refer matters requiring further action to competent investigative, prosecutorial or judicial authorities. Its final report, subject to national security, privacy and witness protection requirements, would be made public and could recommend humanitarian relief, compensation, institutional reforms, legal proceedings and measures to prevent a recurrence. The resolution also urged the AJK government to simultaneously address the people’s legitimate political, economic, administrative and social demands through dialogue and constitutional means, asserting that political disputes should be resolved through negotiations, legal issues through courts and public decisions through the ballot. It concluded by reaffirming the Legislative Assembly’s commitment to peace, democracy, constitutional governance and public rights, condemning all acts of armed violence and disorder and praying for peace, stability and prosperity in the region. After the resolutions were passed, the PML-N’s Nisara Abbasi pointed out the lack of quorum, following which the chair ordered the bells to be rung. Ayoub adjourned the Assembly for 15-20 minutes, but when it assembled again, the attendance showed no improvement, prompting the chair to adjourn the session till Friday.

items.title: Houet : une forte mobilisation citoyenne redonne un nouveau visage à Bama
items.description: Houet : une forte mobilisation citoyenne redonne un nouveau visage à Bama Bama, 30 juil. 2026 (AIB) – La population de la commune de Bama s'est fortement mobilisée, le mardi 28 juillet 2026, à l'occasion d'une journée de salubrité consacrée au curage des caniveaux et à l'assainissement des principaux axes de la ville, dans le but d'améliorer le cadre de vie des habitants en cette saison des pluies. Présidée par le Président de la Délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune, Félix Bayé, l'opération a rassemblé les forces vives locales. Associations et coopératives de jeunes, groupements de femmes, Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), ainsi que de nombreux citoyens ont pris part aux travaux, équipés de pelles, de pioches, de balais et de brouettes. L'activité a bénéficié de la coordination de Sofa Hien, responsable de la Sécurité, de l'Hygiène et de l'Environnement de l'initiative présidentielle Faso Mêbo à Bama, ainsi que d'un appui technique et logistique marqué par la mise à disposition d'engins lourds pour faciliter les travaux. Les équipes ont procédé au dégagement des caniveaux obstrués par le sable et les déchets, rétablissant ainsi l'écoulement normal des eaux pluviales et réduisant les risques d'inondation dans plusieurs secteurs de la commune. À l'ouverture de l'activité, le PDS Félix Bayé a salué la forte mobilisation des populations et félicité particulièrement les jeunes, les femmes ainsi que les FDS pour leur engagement citoyen et leur esprit de patriotisme. Il a invité les riverains à préserver durablement la propreté des ouvrages d'assainissement afin de prévenir les maladies et les désagréments liés aux eaux stagnantes. Les travaux se sont déroulés sous la sécurisation de la Gendarmerie nationale et des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP), qui ont veillé au bon déroulement de l'opération tout au long de la journée. Agence d'information du Burkina BB/AB/wis

items.title: Government proposes 35-year minimum age for presidential candidates, rejects CRC’s 30 years recommendation
items.description: The government has proposed reducing the minimum age for presidential candidates from the current 40 years to 35 years, opting against the Constitutional Review Committee’s recommendation of 30 years. Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr Dominic Ayine, announced the government’s position at a press conference at the Presidency on Thursday, July 30, after the Constitutional Review Committee presented its final report to President John Dramani Mahama. According to Dr Ayine, while the committee recommended lowering the eligibility age for presidential candidates to 30 years, the government believes 35 years is a more appropriate threshold. “The committee recommended that the minimum age for eligibility for election as president be reduced from 40 years currently in the Constitution to 30 years, and the government has accepted this recommendation in principle, subject to one modification. The minimum age will be 35 years, not 30 years,” he said. The recommendation forms part of the Constitutional Review Committee’s broader proposals to amend Ghana’s 1992 Constitution. Chaired by Professor H. Kwasi Prempeh, the committee presented its final report to President Mahama earlier on Thursday at the Jubilee House, outlining reforms covering governance structures, the powers of state institutions and the tenure of elected office holders.

items.title: Adidas apologises for plethora of pink boots at World Cup
items.description: Adidas on Thursday apologised for a surfeit of pink boots at the World Cup, saying that it was a coincidence that they were sported by a striking number of players. Asked by AFP about the unusual uniformity of boot colours during a press conference on the company’s quarterly results, Adidas CEO Bjorn Gulden said “it was an accident”. “I think it’s a coincidence, and I hope it will not happen again,” he added. It was not the colour itself but different brands all opting for the same hue that had surprised him, Gulden said. “Pink is a good colour, no doubt. But that we all ended up with the same is strange,” he said. Various theories have been advanced for the prevalence of pink boots at this year’s World Cup. Some have suggested that pink boots are more visible against a green pitch, helping boot makers’ products stand out to fans. Nike football footwear product manager Odinga Nimako told sports publication The Athletic that pink was preferred by some players as it was seen as an expression of confidence. Boot makers usually had little knowledge of their rivals’ precise colour schemes before new collections are launched, Gulden said. “We don’t have information on what Nike or Puma or New Balance is doing,” he said, adding that retailers could have stepped in. “Retailers normally would tell you: ‘Hang on a minute, you’re all doing the same colour’,” Gulden said. “But we didn’t hear anything. And shame on us, I think no one liked it.” The post Adidas apologises for plethora of pink boots at World Cup appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Budget 2027 : Motaze lance les arbitrages sur la dépense publique utile
items.description: © (DR) Le Ministre des Finances Louis Paul Motaze a ouvert le mardi 28 juillet 2026 à Yaoundé les travaux préparatoires du budget 2027. Objectif : moins de saupoudrage, plus d’investissements qui transforment le quotidien. Les priorités sont déjà tracées : État de service, croissance et pouvoir d’achat. Deux jours pour calibrer les dépenses de toute une année. Réunissant l’ensemble des acteurs de la chaîne budgétaire, le séminaire lancé le mardi 28 juillet 2026 à Yaoundé marque le début officiel de la préparation du budget de l’État pour l’exercice 2027. Le thème donne le cap : « Le budget du Cameroun face aux défis du renforcement de l’État de service, des investissements publics en vue de la stimulation de la croissance et de l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations ». En clair, on sort de la logique comptable pour entrer dans la logique résultat. Trois priorités structurent les arbitrages. Primo: L’État de service. L’administration doit livrer. Il s’agit d’accélérer les délais de paiement, de digitaliser les procédures et de rapprocher les services des usagers. Le budget 2027 devra financer des ministères évalués sur leurs performances, pas seulement sur leurs crédits. Secundo. Investir pour faire croître.Le gros des marges ira aux projets structurants. Routes, énergie, eau, santé et éducation restent en tête. Mais avec une exigence nouvelle : l’optimisation. Fini les chantiers qui dorment. Le cadrage stratégique met l’accent sur les investissements publics à fort effet d’entraînement sur l’économie et l’emploi. Tertio.Protéger le pouvoir d’achat. Dans un contexte de tensions sur les prix, le budget devra aussi amortir les chocs. Subventions ciblées, appui à la production locale, filets sociaux : le gouvernement veut que la croissance se ressente dans les ménages. Pour Louis Paul Motaze, 2027 ne sera pas un budget de continuité mécanique. Ce sera un budget de choix. Chaque ministère devra justifier l’utilité de sa dépense. Chaque projet devra prouver son impact. Les deux jours d’échanges permettront de poser les grands équilibres et les cadrages macroéconomiques. Ensuite viendront les conférences budgétaires, ministère par ministère. Le message est passé : en 2027, l’argent public devra servir à produire de la croissance et à améliorer concrètement la vie des Camerounais. Cet article Budget 2027 : Motaze lance les arbitrages sur la dépense publique utile est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Remi Tinubu seeks Western education for Almajiri children
items.description: The First Lady, Sen. Oluremi Tinubu, has called for greater support to ensure that Almajiri and out-of-school children have access to formal education that combines Arabic instruction with Western education.‎ Tinubu made the call on Thursday in Abuja while receiving the new Saudi Arabian Ambassador to Nigeria, Amb. Yousef bin Mohammed Albalawi, and the embassy’s Chief of Staff, Mr Mohammed Bukar. She said that formal education would improve the children’s standard of living and help secure Nigeria’s future. The First Lady called for a strategic partnership between Nigeria and Saudi Arabia to reform the Almajiri education system by integrating Islamic teachings with formal Western education. She said the collaboration would help address the challenges facing Almajiri and out-of-school children while protecting the future of vulnerable children across the country. Tinubu noted that Nigeria and Saudi Arabia had maintained cordial relations over the years and appreciated the ambassador for the visit. “I work with women and vulnerable children in society, and my heart goes out to the Almajiri children in the North. I believe they need better care. “This is because most of the insecurity challenges in the nation, if that particular group of children are not taken care of, I don’t know what might happen. “I believe we can still start begin to give them formal education. If we are able to do that, the future of Nigeria will be well secured, ” Tinubu said. Earlier, Albalawi, who said he had spent only five months in Nigeria, expressed satisfaction with the warm reception accorded him by government officials. He said he had met with members of the Federal Executive Council and expressed confidence that the engagements would strengthen bilateral relations and promote the growth of both countries. The ambassador said he looked forward to deeper cooperation that would enhance the economic development of Nigeria and Saudi Arabia. “As you are aware, our countries have a strong relationship; we both share a historical relationship, our nations share a lot of things- religion, culture and potential to improve our relationship to get back in shape. ‎”Our nations have strong ambitions to improve our economy.” The post Remi Tinubu seeks Western education for Almajiri children appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NMDPRA seeks West African benchmark for petroleum products pricing
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) has called on petroleum regulators across West Africa to collaborate on establishing a regional pricing benchmark for refined petroleum products. The authority said a transparent West African pricing mechanism would strengthen market confidence, promote cross-border trade and attract investment into the downstream petroleum sector. The Chief Executive of NMDPRA, Rabiu Umar, made the call in Abuja on Thursday ahead of the second West Africa Refined Fuel Conference. Umar argued that Africa, despite being a major producer of crude oil and natural gas, still relies heavily on international markets to determine the prices of petroleum products produced within the continent. He said the conference, organised in partnership with S&P Global Commodity Insights and the West Africa Regulators Forum (WARF), was aimed at developing a credible regional marketplace where petroleum products could be traded efficiently, transparently and competitively. “The vision is to establish West Africa as a credible regional marketplace where petroleum products can be traded efficiently, transparently and competitively,” Umar said. “By strengthening infrastructure, harmonising regulations and improving market data, the region can enhance price discovery, facilitate cross-border trade and attract greater investment.” The conference, scheduled for August 11 and 12 in Abuja, is themed: “Funding West Africa Infrastructure & Distribution to Create a Transparent Market for Regional Price Benchmarks.” It will bring together regulators, investors, financial institutions and industry stakeholders to explore ways of financing infrastructure and logistics required to support a regional petroleum trading hub. Umar said progress had been recorded since the maiden edition of the conference in 2025, including the establishment of the West Africa Regulators Forum, publication of West African reference prices and the opening of S&P Global Commodity Insights’ regional office in Abuja. He said the 2026 edition would focus on infrastructure financing, regional cooperation, market transparency, logistics development and expanding refining capacity to improve energy security and reduce dependence on imported petroleum products. The NMDPRA chief identified pipelines, storage facilities, marine terminals, ports, rail infrastructure, digital commodity exchanges, trading platforms, strategic petroleum reserves, LNG infrastructure and logistics corridors as critical investments needed to create an integrated regional energy market. He also highlighted opportunities across the gas value chain, including gas processing, transportation, liquefaction and compression. Umar stressed that regulators had a key role in ensuring fair competition, investor confidence, consumer protection and regional cooperation through harmonised standards and regulations. He defended the need for a regional petroleum products pricing benchmark, noting that major energy markets across the world operate reference pricing systems that reflect their local realities. He cited the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) trading hub in Europe as an example of a benchmark that considers supply, demand, transportation and logistics costs. “The more we are able to produce, the more relevant it becomes to have our own reference pricing,” he said. Umar added that infrastructure remained central to regional energy integration, noting that pipelines, ports and storage facilities were essential for efficient movement of petroleum products across borders. He also called for the harmonisation of petroleum product specifications across African countries to boost regional trade, adding that ongoing engagements with stakeholders, including the Africa Refiners Association, were making progress. According to him, petroleum products supplied from Nigeria meet international quality standards, with sulphur content not exceeding 50 parts per million, while increased domestic refining capacity is improving local supply and supporting exports to neighbouring countries. items.title: Bénin : le Sénat s’installe entre réforme institutionnelle et retour des anciens présidents
items.description: Le Benin a officiellement installe son Senat, ce 30 juillet a Porto-Novo. Cette chambre haute du Parlement a ete creee a la faveur de la revision constitutionnelle adoptee en novembre 2025 sous la presidence de Patrice Talon. Si la ceremonie d'installation s'est tenue dans la capitale politique, les senateurs exerceront leurs fonctions a Cotonou. Composee de 25 membres designes ou siegeant de droit, l'institution ne compte aucun elu au suffrage direct, un point qui avait nourri les critiques de l'opposition lors de l'adoption de la reforme. Le parti d'opposition Les Democrates s'etait oppose au projet. Son ancien president, Boni Yayi, membre de droit du Senat, avait d'abord refuse d'y sieger avant de revenir sur sa decision. Il a finalement accepte de rejoindre l'institution, qu'il presente comme « l'un des rares espaces de debat qui reste », avec l'intention d'y defendre les libertes publiques, la democratie ainsi que le sort des personnalites politiques emprisonnees ou en exil. L'influence de l'ancien president en question L'installation du Senat relance egalement le debat sur l'influence de Patrice Talon depuis son depart du pouvoir, il y a deux mois. Selon ses adversaires, cette institution lui offre un moyen de continuer a peser sur la vie politique. L'ancien chef de l'etat avait toutefois defendu ce role avant de quitter la presidence, estimant qu'il serait « une faute de se derober » lorsqu'il s'agit de mettre son experience au service du pays. Outre Patrice Talon et Boni Yayi, le Senat accueille egalement Nicephore Soglo, âge de 95 ans. Doyen de l'institution, il est le troisieme ancien president de la Republique a y sieger de droit. Parmi les autres personnalites figurent les anciens presidents de la Cour constitutionnelle Robert Dossou et Theodore Holo, les anciens presidents de l'Assemblee nationale Adrien Houngbedji et Bruno Amoussou, ainsi qu'Ousmane Batoko, ancien president de la Cour supreme. La seance inaugurale doit se limiter a un discours d'installation et a l'adoption du reglement interieur. Le bureau sera elu apres la validation de ce texte par la Cour constitutionnelle.

items.title: Écologie et climat : Yaoundé I se dote d’une Chaire UNESCO
items.description: © DR Inaugurée le lundi 27 juillet 2026, la nouvelle Chaire UNESCO de l’Université de Yaoundé I veut faire de la recherche camerounaise un levier pour le développement durable. Placée sous la tutelle du Pr Laurent Serge Etoundi Ngoa, elle se donne pour mission de modéliser les systèmes naturels et de proposer des réponses concrètes aux crises environnementales. L’Université de Yaoundé I entre dans une nouvelle dimension. Le lundi 27 juillet 2026, la cérémonie solennelle d’inauguration de sa Chaire UNESCO s’est tenue sur le campus, sous la conduite du Pr Laurent Serge Etoundi Ngoa, Ministre de l’Éducation de Base et Président de la Commission Nationale pour l’UNESCO du Cameroun. L’enjeu affiché est clair : placer l’institution au cœur de la recherche appliquée sur l’écologie. La chaire sera axée sur trois piliers la modélisation écologique, le développement durable et la géoscience. Autrement dit, comprendre comment fonctionnent les forêts, les bassins, les sols, pour mieux anticiper sécheresses, inondations et perte de biodiversité. La présence était à la hauteur. À ses côtés, le Pr Jacques Fame Ndongo, Ministre d’État, Ministre de l’Enseignement Supérieur. Également présents : André-Magnus Ekoumou, Délégué Permanent du Cameroun auprès de l’UNESCO, et le Pr Remy Magloire Dieudonné Etoua, Recteur de Yaoundé I et premier titulaire de la Chaire. L’initiative porte la marque du patron de l’Éducation de Base. C’est sous son impulsion que le dossier a été porté jusqu’à Paris. L’objectif n’est pas de produire des thèses pour les bibliothèques. La Commission Nationale UNESCO veut des modèles utilisables : cartes de vulnérabilité, outils d’aide à la décision pour les collectivités, données exploitables par les ministères techniques. Pour le Pr Etoua, la chaire doit devenir un carrefour. Chercheurs, étudiants, ONG et secteur privé sont invités à travailler ensemble. Le Cameroun, avec son bassin du Congo, sa façade atlantique et ses savanes, offre un terrain d’observation unique. Dans un contexte où le climat dérègle les calendriers agricoles et fragilise les villes, Yaoundé I se positionne. Pas comme une université de plus, mais comme un centre capable d’exporter de l’expertise. La chaire est lancée. Reste maintenant à transformer les équations en solutions. Cet article Écologie et climat : Yaoundé I se dote d’une Chaire UNESCO est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Última hora de los incendios forestales, en directo | Sánchez anuncia el fin de la emergencia nacional en Ávila y Madrid
items.description: El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, ha anunciado este jueves el fin de la emergencia nacional declarada en el incendio de Ávila y Madrid. Sánchez considera que la respuesta ha sido “eficaz a la envergadura del incendio”, en una visita al Puesto de Mando Avanzado del municipio abulense de Navaluenga. Mientras, en Castilla y León, 10 incendios activos, tres de nivel de peligrosidad máximo en Fermoselle (Zamora) y Veguellina y Valdelaloba, en León, asedian la comunidad en el arranque de este jueves, en medio de la segunda jornada de la cuarta ola de calor del verano. La noche ha sido especialmente larga y complicada en Zamora, donde más de medio centenar de medios terrestres y aéreos, con apoyo de la UME, luchan contra el fuego que se originó ayer en Fermoselle, en las Arribes del Duero. El fuego ha arrasado 11.000 hectáreas en un día, ha obligado a desalojar 14 localidades con más de 800 personas y a confinar Fermoselle y Fariza. El operativo de extinción teme especialmente el viento que está previsto que se avive durante la tarde de este jueves y las altas temperaturas. Además, este jueves continúan las tareas de contención de los incendios ya estabilizados de Ávila, Madrid y Toledo para evitar reinicios, sin descuidar otros focos activos como el de Castellón o Tarragona, en horas críticas para un país expuesto a los efectos de la nueva ola de calor. items.title: Government backs five-year presidential and parliamentary term proposal
items.description: The government has accepted a recommendation by the Constitutional Review Committee to extend the tenure of the President and Members of Parliament from four years to five years, arguing that the current constitutional cycle does not provide enough time for governments to effectively implement their programmes. Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr Dominic Ayine, announced the government’s position at a press conference at the Presidency on Thursday, July 30, shortly after the Constitutional Review Committee presented its final report to President John Dramani Mahama at the Jubilee House. According to Dr Ayine, the government believes a five-year mandate would provide a more practical timeframe for policy formulation, implementation and evaluation, while reducing the impact of the country’s frequent election cycle on governance. He explained that under the existing four-year term, a significant portion of every administration is spent on transition and election-related activities, leaving limited time to deliver on campaign promises. “The government has accepted the recommendation to extend the term of office of the president from four years to five years with the term of parliament extended to correspond with this. Our thinking is practical. Under the current four-year cycle, the early months of every administration are consumed by transition and the final year is consumed by election. A five-year term provides a more realistic timeframe for the formulation, implementation and the assessment of every government,” Dr Ayine said. The proposal forms part of a broader package of constitutional reforms contained in the final report of the Constitutional Review Committee, chaired by Professor H. Kwasi Prempeh. The report, presented to President Mahama on Thursday, contains recommendations aimed at reviewing Ghana’s 1992 Constitution, including proposals affecting governance structures, the powers of state institutions and the tenure of elected office holders.

items.description: By Peter Egwuatu Femi Otedola, Chairman of First HoldCo Plc, has increased his stake in the financial institution after acquiring additional 1.779 billion shares valued at N222.209 billion. The acquisition was disclosed in a statement signed by the company’s Secretary, Abiola Baruwa, and filed with the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) on Thursday. According to the statement, the shares were purchased through Otedola’s investment vehicle, Calvados Global Services Limited, at N124.90 per share. The latest transaction increased Otedola’s holdings in First HoldCo from 9.99 billion shares to 11.77 billion shares, raising his stake from 21.96 per cent to approximately 26 per cent. The acquisition marks the second major share purchase by Otedola in First HoldCo in July 2026. On July 22, 2026, he acquired 706.13 million shares of the company valued at N77.58 billion. With the latest purchase, Otedola’s investment in First HoldCo has risen to about N1.47 trillion, making him the largest individual investor in the financial institution. items.title: Pression migratoire : Sebta face à une vague d'ampleur inédite
items.description: La ville de Sebta fait face à une vague de migration d'une ampleur inédite, marquée par des tentatives massives de traversée depuis le littoral nord. Le littoral nord du Royaume fait face à une période de forte tension marquée par une vague de migration d'une ampleur inédite entre Fnideq et l'enclave occupée de Sebta. Face à la multiplication des tentatives de traversée maritime, la réponse s'organise avec fermeté sur le terrain pour contenir les flux, maintenir l'ordre public et contrecarrer les agissements des réseaux criminels. Verrouillage sécuritaire et fermetures préventives à Fnideq Sur le terrain, les autorités marocaines ont déployé un dispositif de surveillance d'envergure. À Fnideq, l'ensemble des forces de l'ordre ( Sûreté nationale, Gendarmerie royale, Forces auxiliaires et autorités locales ) a été mobilisé le long du littoral et sur les axes menant au poste-frontière de Bab Sebta. Par mesure de précaution pour empêcher tout départ clandestin, l'accès aux plages de la zone a été totalement interdit au public. Cette présence renforcée a déjà permis d'intercepter et d'éloigner plus de 1 500 candidats à l'émigration irrégulière. En mer, les patrouilles de la Marine royale, de la Gendarmerie maritime et de la Protection civile opèrent en permanence pour secourir les personnes en difficulté et intercepter les traversées à la nage. Les réseaux de passeurs dans le collimateur Face à la recrudescence de ces tentatives, la diplomatie marocaine est fermement montée au créneau pour recadrer la situation. Selon des sources de l'ambassade du Royaume à Madrid, citées par l'agence Europa Press, ces mouvements ne reflètent en aucun cas une volonté des autorités de favoriser l'immigration irrégulière. Tout indique qu'ils procèdent d'une exploitation cynique menée par des organisations criminelles de traite d'êtres humains. Ces filières mafieuses profitent de la vulnérabilité des migrants en alimentant de fausses attentes, notamment en instrumentalisant le récent arrêt du Tribunal suprême espagnol sur les procédures de renvoi en mer. Réaffirmant que le Maroc « ne favorise ni n'encourage l'immigration irrégulière de ses ressortissants » , Rabat souligne sa position de partenaire « stratégique, fiable et responsable ». Le Royaume déploie des efforts soutenus pour démanteler ces réseaux et prévenir les départs, conformément à la vision royale d'une gestion migratoire solidaire, humaine et respectueuse de l'État de droit. Madrid rejette l'état d'urgence Du côté espagnol, alors que les autorités locales de Sebta réclamaient la déclaration d'« urgence d'intérêt national », le gouvernement central a opposé une fin de non-recevoir. Madrid a fait savoir que la gestion des flux migratoires ne relève pas du cadre juridique de la protection civile, privilégiant plutôt l'envoi de renforts logistiques et d'effectifs supplémentaires sur le terrain. L'exécutif espagnol a par ailleurs souligné que l'intervention des forces marocaines permet de bloquer l'arrivée d'un nombre important de personnes. C'est dans ce contexte de vive tension que s'inscrit la visite sur place du ministre espagnol de l'Intérieur, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, venu évaluer la situation opérationnelle. Au cours de la semaine du 20 au 26 juillet 2026, les équipes de la Brigade communale d’embellissement ont mis en terre 502 plants sur l'avenue Issa Hayatou, le boulevard de la Révolution, la RN8 (route de Bama) et le terre-plein central de l'avenue de la Liberté. Selon la Commune, cette initiative vise à accroître le couvert végétal, embellir les espaces publics et contribuer à la lutte contre les effets du changement climatique. Créée en mars 2026, la Brigade d’embellissement est chargée de conduire les actions de végétalisation et d'entretien des espaces verts sur le territoire communal. Le président de la Délégation spéciale communale, Laurent Kontogom, a invité les habitants à protéger les jeunes plants et à participer à leur entretien. Pour lui, la sauvegarde du patrimoine végétal est une responsabilité collective indispensable à la construction d'une ville plus verte, plus attractive et durable. items.title: FCCPC seeks unified consumer protection rules as states open electricity markets
items.description: By Progress Godfrey ABUJA — The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) has called for stronger collaboration and harmonised regulatory frameworks among electricity sector regulators as states begin to establish and operate their own electricity markets. The Executive Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of FCCPC, Mr Tunji Bello, said the implementation of the Electricity Act, 2023, had significantly altered Nigeria’s electricity regulatory landscape by empowering states to establish electricity regulatory commissions and oversee intrastate electricity markets. Bello spoke at a stakeholder engagement on Consumer Protection and Regulatory Cooperation in Nigeria’s Electricity Sector held at the FCCPC headquarters in Abuja on Thursday. The meeting brought together officials from the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC), Nigerian Electricity Management Services Agency (NEMSA), and State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs). He said the changing regulatory environment required cooperation among agencies with different but complementary responsibilities. “Sector regulators bring deep technical expertise, while the FCCPC brings economy-wide experience in consumer protection and competition. Within the electricity sector, NERC provides sector-specific regulation, NEMSA enforces technical standards, the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions undertake intrastate regulation and the FCCPC contributes its cross-sector consumer protection mandate,” Bello said. According to him, effective regulatory governance requires consultation, information sharing and mutual support among regulators to ensure consumers receive timely and effective protection. The FCCPC boss said consumer protection should go beyond resolving disputes after they occur, stressing the need for preventive measures, early identification of risks and actions that would sustain public confidence in the electricity sector. He cited the commission’s 2024 intervention over the planned replacement of obsolete Unistar prepaid meters as an example of effective regulatory collaboration. Bello explained that the intervention followed concerns that consumers might bear the cost of meter replacements or face estimated billing and power supply disruptions. “The obsolete meter intervention illustrates an important principle. The Commission respected NERC’s statutory mandate and recognised its technical expertise. We did not seek to assume the role of the sector regulator. Instead, we acted in a way that supported the existing regulatory framework and strengthened its effectiveness,” he said. Also speaking, Assistant Director and Head of Consumer Protection Department at NERC, Anthony Essien, said regulatory convergence was essential to protect consumers across Nigeria’s emerging federal, state and regional electricity markets. Essien noted that while state electricity markets would bring regulation closer to consumers, inconsistent standards across states could pose challenges for investors. “Having a convergence like this is very paramount to foster collaboration and coordinated efforts towards serving the different electricity markets that have been created,” he said. He added that harmonised regulatory approaches would strengthen the mandates of regulators and provide a coordinated framework for electricity market development across the country. The Executive Commissioner of Anambra State Electricity Regulatory Commission (ASERC), Dr Nnaemeka Ewelukwa, said the Electricity Act 2023 and the constitutional amendment preceding it had created opportunities for states to play a greater role in electricity regulation. Ewelukwa said the emergence of state regulators would improve consumer engagement and create a more direct relationship between investors and state authorities. He added that closer cooperation among state regulators, FCCPC and NERC would reduce regulatory burdens for investors operating across multiple states by limiting variations in requirements. items.title: Think before you type: Respect must extend online
items.description: Social media has transformed how Ghanaians communicate, learn, work, build relationships and participate in public life. Yet the growth of digital communication must be matched by a stronger sense of responsibility. Cyberbullying can take many forms: abusive comments, threats, impersonation, body-shaming, deliberate humiliation, repeated harassment and the sharing of embarrassing or private content without consent. Too often, these actions are dismissed as jokes, trolling or “catching cruise.” But a comment typed in seconds can remain online for years and affect someone’s confidence, education, career, relationships and emotional wellbeing. Respect online does not mean avoiding disagreement. Social media should remain a space where people can challenge misinformation, criticise decisions and debate difficult issues. However, disagreement should not become insults, tribal attacks, sexual harassment, threats or attacks on a person’s appearance, family or identity. Strong opinions can still be expressed with dignity. Bystanders also have a role. Liking, forwarding, reposting or laughing at humiliating content can amplify the harm. Silence can also allow abusive behaviour to continue. Users can help by refusing to share harmful material, reporting abusive posts and checking on the person being targeted. Those experiencing cyberbullying should preserve evidence, take screenshots, block or mute abusive accounts and use in-app reporting tools. They should also speak to trusted relatives, teachers, counsellors, colleagues or friends. Serious threats, impersonation and the non-consensual sharing of private material should be reported to the appropriate authorities. Schools, families, media organisations and social-media platforms also have responsibilities. Digital citizenship education, accessible reporting systems and supportive conversations can help prevent abuse and protect victims. The Think Before You Type initiative continues to promote safer digital spaces through social-media education, media engagement and direct outreach to young people. Its message is simple: behind every username is a real person, and every post, comment and share contributes to the culture we create online. Before publishing anything, ask: Is it true? Is it necessary? Is it respectful? Could it cause avoidable harm? A screen may create distance, but it does not remove responsibility. Pause. Reflect. Think before you type.

items.title: NAPTIP reunites 258 trafficking victims, records 78 cases in Jigawa
items.description: The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), says it has recorded 78 cases, rescued and reunited 258 victims with their families in the last three years in Jigawa. The NAPTIP Commander in the state, Mr Abdulkadir Turajo, made this known on Thursday in Dutse in a statement to commemorate the 2026 World Day Against Trafficking in Persons. Turajo said a total of 512 migrants who are indigene of the state were also returned from different countries by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) between January 2025 and July 2026. He explained that the command also secured two convictions, including that of a foreign national, within the period under The commander added that the agency has conducted 150 sensitisation campaigns in schools, communities, markets and worship places across the 27 LGAs of the state. “The command also conducted six sensitisation campaigns to commemorate the 2026 Day in Kazaure and Roni LGAs, being some of the most trafficking in persons areas in Jigawa State. “The Command wishes to use this medium to send a strong warning to all traffickers, both within and from outside, wishing to use the state as a source, route or destination for their illicit activities to desist from doing so, as we are ever ready and capable of dealing decisively with anybody or group of people that try to engage in human trafficking within the state. “We have a mandate, and we shall discharge it to the letter for the overall good of the state and the nation at large,” the commander said Turajo further urged the public to support the agency by reporting all suspected cases of human trafficking, child abuse and other related offences to the state command headquarters at Block 5 Old State Secretariat, Dutse or via 0904 964 3905, infojigawa@naptip.gov.ng, 627 short code and through the NAPTIP iReporter APP on Android and ios. He also enjoined people to desist from hiding information or harboring people that are engaging in human trafficking and related offences. The commander, who appreciated the state government for all its support and cooperation, lauded Gov. Umar Namadi for his commitment and support to the war against human trafficking. “We equally appreciate security agencies and all other partners in the state for their support. We urge you all to join hands with NAPTIP in this collective fight against our common enemy.” The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the theme for the 2026 World Day Against Trafficking is “Trapped Behind The Scam’’ which calls for accelerated action to end human trafficking, highlighting the fake job advertisements, scam compounds and all cyber-enabled fraud used by traffickers to lure the vulnerable victims into illicit trafficking activities. items.title: Ebonyi warns against encroachment on government lands
items.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Government has warned individuals encroaching on Development Centre lands and other government-owned properties in the state to desist or face legal action. The State Commissioner for Lands and Survey, Dr. Matthew Nwobasi, gave the warning during a meeting with coordinators of the 64 Development Centres in the state at his office in Centenary City, Abakaliki. Nwobasi disclosed that several Development Centre lands had been encroached upon and directed those involved to vacate the properties immediately. He reminded the coordinators that Development Centres were established by the state government through legislation and were not under the control of local government authorities. According to him, coordinators are expected to hand over to their successors at the end of their tenure and not to local government chairmen unless otherwise directed by the state government. The commissioner urged coordinators who had not surveyed their lands to do so immediately and ensure that copies of the survey plans were submitted to the Ministry of Lands and Survey. He said the ministry would embark on inspections of Development Centres across the state to assess the level of encroachment and ensure compliance with government directives. “Any Development Centre visited and it is discovered that the coordinator is not doing anything serious to prevent encroachment will be treated as a collaborator,” he warned. Nwobasi further directed coordinators whose lands had already been surveyed but encroached upon to take immediate steps to recover the properties. Also speaking, the Surveyor-General of the state, Surv. Dr. John Igbede, said clearly defined boundaries for Development Centre lands would help promote peaceful relationships between the centres, host communities and other stakeholders. He explained that when the Development Centres were created, communities willingly provided lands for their establishment but that the boundaries had gradually been reduced through encroachments over time. Igbede stressed the need for proper demarcation and mapping of the lands to prevent disputes and protect government properties. Some coordinators, including Hon. John Nwofoke of Abakaliki Development Centre, Hon. Chukwuemeka Ali of Ishielu West Development Centre and Engr. Okoronkwo Ozioma Raphael of Okposi Development Centre, commended the commissioner for the engagement and appealed to the ministry to assist in recovering lands taken over by encroachers. items.title: Sénégal : le conflit autour de Pape Thiaw prend de l'ampleur
items.description: Quelques semaines après le limogeage de Pape Thiaw, une nouvelle crise secoue le football sénégalais. Le différend opposant l'ancien sélectionneur des Lions de la Teranga à la Fédération sénégalaise de football (FSF) continue de s'envenimer, sur fond de désaccord avec le gouvernement concernant son contrat, au point de faire planer la menace d'une procédure judiciaire. Selon RMC Sport, citant le quotidien sénégalais Sud Quotidien, le ministère sénégalais de la Jeunesse, des Sports et de la Culture a officiellement informé la FSF qu'il n'avait jamais validé la prolongation de trois ans accordée à Pape Thiaw, ni la revalorisation salariale négociée pendant la Coupe du monde 2026. Cette décision place la Fédération dans une situation délicate. L'État, qui prend en charge une partie des engagements financiers liés au sélectionneur, refuse désormais de financer ce nouveau contrat, ouvrant la voie à un bras de fer administratif et juridique. Quelques jours avant son licenciement, le 12 juillet, Pape Thiaw avait signé un nouveau contrat. Son renouvellement avait toutefois suscité une vive controverse durant le Mondial 2026, marqué par plusieurs tensions au sein de la délégation sénégalaise, tant sur le plan administratif que logistique. Le président de la Fédération sénégalaise, Abdoulaye Fall, affirme que le technicien avait menacé de ne pas accompagner la sélection à la Coupe du monde si ses exigences financières n'étaient pas satisfaites. Selon lui, le président sénégalais Bassirou Diomaye Faye avait dû intervenir personnellement pour convaincre le sélectionneur de rejoindre la délégation avant son départ vers les États-Unis. Toujours selon Abdoulaye Fall, Pape Thiaw aurait également refusé de prendre place sur le banc de touche avant le match contre la Norvège, le 23 juin, jusqu'à la signature officielle de son nouveau contrat. D'après Sud Quotidien, cet accord prévoyait un salaire mensuel de 30 millions de francs CFA, une prime à la signature de 120 millions de francs CFA, un bonus équivalant à 1 % des primes versées par la FIFA à la sélection sénégalaise, ainsi qu'une indemnité correspondant à huit mois de salaire en cas de rupture du contrat. De nouvelles menaces alimentent la crise Selon plusieurs médias sénégalais, Pape Thiaw aurait également menacé de révéler publiquement les coulisses de la finale de la CAN disputée contre le Maroc s'il ne percevait pas les sommes qu'il estime lui être dues au titre de son contrat. Ces déclarations, si elles étaient confirmées, ajoutent une nouvelle dimension à un dossier déjà explosif, alors que les relations entre l'ancien sélectionneur, la Fédération sénégalaise et les autorités gouvernementales demeurent extrêmement tendues. Le règlement de ce litige financier reste suspendu au refus du gouvernement de prendre en charge les engagements contractuels contestés. Si aucun compromis n'est trouvé dans les prochaines semaines, l'affaire pourrait être portée devant les tribunaux, avec des conséquences importantes pour la Fédération sénégalaise de football. The post Sénégal : le conflit autour de Pape Thiaw prend de l'ampleur appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ghana records GH¢148.3bn trade surplus in 2025 as gold dominates exports
items.description: Ghana recorded a strong performance in international merchandise trade in 2025, posting a trade surplus of GH¢148.3 billion (US$11.5 billion), more than three times the surplus recorded in 2024, driven largely by gold exports and expanding trade relations across global markets. The latest Annual International Merchandise Trade Statistics Report released by the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS) showed that the country’s total trade value reached GH¢654.7 billion (US$52.5 billion) in 2025. According to the report, total exports amounted to GH¢401.5 billion (US$32.0 billion), significantly outpacing imports, which stood at GH¢253.2 billion (US$20.5 billion). The resulting trade surplus represents one of Ghana’s strongest trade performances in recent years. Gold continued to dominate Ghana’s export basket, generating GH¢252.4 billion and accounting for nearly 63 percent of the country’s total export earnings in 2025. Together with cocoa products and mineral fuels, the three commodities contributed 85.9 percent of Ghana’s total exports during the year. The report highlights Ghana’s continued dependence on primary commodities despite efforts to diversify exports, with gold remaining the country’s single largest foreign exchange earner. Ghana also strengthened its global trade footprint in 2025 by increasing the number of countries it traded with. The country imported goods from 216 countries, up from 211 in 2024, while exports reached 163 countries compared to 155 in the previous year. Asia remained Ghana’s largest trading region, reflecting the country’s growing commercial ties with Asian economies. Trade with African countries, however, remained favourable to Ghana, with exports to the continent more than twice the value of imports from African nations, reinforcing Ghana’s position as a net exporter within Africa. The Ghana Statistical Service reported that the country recorded a trade surplus of GH¢34.7 billion with African countries in 2025. Food exports also experienced significant growth during the period, driven by increased exports of cocoa products, cashew nuts, tuna and shea products. At the same time, food imports declined slightly, suggesting improved performance in some segments of Ghana’s agricultural and agro-processing sectors. On the import front, China maintained its position as Ghana’s largest source of imports in 2025, with imports from the Asian giant exceeding GH¢57 billion. Fuel products continued to account for a substantial share of the country’s import bill. Diesel and petrol imports alone exceeded GH¢51 billion during the year, underscoring Ghana’s continued reliance on imported petroleum products despite domestic refining efforts. Government Statistician, Dr. Alhassan Iddrisu, said the figures contained in the 2025 Annual International Merchandise Trade Statistics Report reflect the country’s expanding participation in global trade and its growing export competitiveness, particularly within the African market. The report further points to the importance of commodity exports in sustaining Ghana’s trade surplus, while highlighting opportunities for export diversification and value addition to strengthen the country’s long-term trade resilience.

items.title: État stratège, Souveraineté et Nouveau contrat social : anatomie du discours du Trône 2026
items.description: Il est des discours qui font office de bilan, et d’autres qui dessinent les contours d’une nouvelle ère. Le Discours du Trône prononcé le 29 juillet 2026 par le Roi Mohammed VI appartient incontestablement à la seconde catégorie. À l’aube de sa 28e année de règne, le Souverain a livré une leçon magistrale de philosophie politique et de pragmatisme économique, actant la mutation du Maroc : d’une nation en quête d’émergence à une puissance de souveraineté et de résilience, naviguant avec assurance dans un monde en pleine polycrise. Loin de la rhétorique triomphaliste, ce discours s'impose comme un manifeste de l’« État-Strège » marocain. En croisant les dimensions sociales, économiques et géopolitiques, il révèle une doctrine de pouvoir fondée sur trois piliers : la stabilité comme arme absolue, l'autosuffisance stratégique comme dogme, et la dignité du citoyen comme unique boussole. La Déconstruction de l’égo géopolitique au profit du contrat social La phrase d'ouverture du discours résonne comme une rupture philosophique avec les archétypes du pouvoir dans la région MENA : « Jamais la poursuite d’une gloire personnelle, ni l’envie de consécration par le titre de Leader continental ou international n’ont été une fin pour Moi» . Par cette déclaration, le Roi Mohammed VI opère une déconstruction radicale du culte de l'ego géopolitique. Il recentre la légitimité de l'État non pas sur le prestige international ou la projection de puissance, mais sur l'accomplissement d'un contrat social renouvelé. Cette vision lockienne et rousseauiste, adaptée aux constantes nationales, place la « dignité » et la « liberté » du citoyen au sommet de la pyramide des priorités. C’est dans cette logique que s'inscrit la généralisation de la protection sociale, qui n'est plus vue comme une simple politique publique, mais comme le fondement moral de l'État marocain contemporain. La Stabilité : de la « denrée rare » à l'atout stratégique Dans un contexte mondial marqué par le retour de la guerre en Europe, les tensions au Moyen-Orient et les fractures sahéliennes, le Roi pose un constat lucide : « la stabilité politique et institutionnelle constitue une denrée rare et un atout d’une valeur inestimable » . L'analyse académique de cette affirmation est primordiale. Le Maroc ne considère plus la stabilité comme un simple acquis pacifique, mais comme sa principale variable d'ajustement économique. C'est cette stabilité qui a permis au Royaume d'absorber les chocs exogènes (crises sanitaires, disruptions des chaînes logistiques mondiales) et endogènes (gestion des inondations du Gharb). Le discours révèle que l'institution monarchique agit comme un « stabilisateur automatique » face aux convulsions régionales, offrant aux investisseurs et aux partenaires une prévisibilité qui fait cruellement défaut aux marchés émergents concurrents. L’économie de la souveraineté : le changement de paradigme Sur le plan macroéconomique, le discours acte la fin d'un cycle et le début d'un autre. Le Maroc n'est plus seulement une plateforme d'exportation ou un hub d'assemblage, il est entré dans l'ère de la souveraineté industrielle et technologique. Les chiffres avancés sont le symptôme d'une métamorphose structurelle : – Le basculement des moteurs de l'export : avec plus de 40% des exportations, l'automobile (1 million de véhicules) et l'aéronautique (moteurs et systèmes d'atterrissage) ont détrôné le phosphate historique. Le Maroc s'est inséré dans les chaînes de valeur les plus exigeantes de la planète. – L'anticipation technologique : le pari sur les batteries électriques et l'hydrogène vert montre une vision à long terme qui dépasse les cycles politiques courts. – La souveraineté de défense : l'annonce la plus lourde de sens géopolitique concerne « l’installation d’une base industrielle et technologique de défense et de cybersécurité ». C'est un signal fort envoyé aux alliés comme aux rivaux : le Maroc entend sécuriser ses propres données, protéger ses infrastructures critiques et maîtriser son destin sécuritaire sans dépendre exclusivement des fournisseurs étrangers. L’impératif de l’autosuffisance et la résilience climatique Le discours met en lumière un nouveau dogme né des crises récentes : l'autosuffisance stratégique. Le fait que les industries agroalimentaires et pharmaceutiques couvrent « près de 80% des besoins nationaux » est une prouesse de souveraineté sanitaire et alimentaire. De plus, la mention de la « sécurité hydrique et alimentaire » face à une bonne campagne agricole, couplée à la gestion des inondations, démontre que le Maroc a intégré la variable climatique non plus comme une fatalité, mais comme un paramètre de planification stratégique. Le Royaume apprend à danser avec la météo, transformant ses vulnérabilités en opportunités d'innovation (dessalement, agriculture smart, gestion des barrages). Le nerf de la guerre : la mobilisation du capital domestique L'un des messages les plus directs et cinglants du discours s'adresse au secteur financier. En exhortant les banques et les institutions à « mobiliser l’épargne nationale » et à élargir l'accès aux financements pour les PME et l'innovation, le Roi pointe du doigt un goulot d'étranglement structurel. L'analyse est claire : le Maroc ne peut plus financer son émergence uniquement par la dette extérieure ou les IDE (Investissements Directs Étrangers). L'heure est au « patriotisme financier » et à la modernisation des marchés de capitaux. Le Souverain demande au système financier de sortir de sa zone de confort (le financement de la consommation et de l'immobilier) pour devenir le moteur de l'industrialisation et de l'innovation. C'est un appel à la responsabilité historique du capital national. La continuité de l'État face à l'alternance politique Enfin, la conclusion du discours contient un message politique subtil mais ferme à l'adresse de la classe politique. En évoquant les prochaines législatives et le futur gouvernement, le Roi rappelle que les « acquis transcendent les mandats gouvernemental et parlementaire ». Il s'agit d'une leçon de science politique : la vision stratégique de l'État (le « Temps Long ») doit primer sur le temps court de l'alternance partisane. Le Roi fixe ici les « lignes rouges » et le cap du prochain exécutif : il ne s'agira pas de réinventer la roue, mais de « préserver les acquis » et d'accélérer les réformes. C'est la consécration du modèle marocain où la Monarchie assure la continuité de l'État et la cohérence des politiques publiques, tandis que le gouvernement est sommé d'être un exécutant rigoureux et un gestionnaire efficient. Le Maroc de 2026, une puissance d'équilibre En 27 ans, le Roi Mohammed VI a réussi ce que peu de leaders au Sud ont accompli : transformer un pays de transit en un pays de destination, et une nation périphérique en un acteur central des équilibres euro-africains. Le discours du 29 juillet 2026 n'est pas celui d'un monarque qui regarde dans le rétroviseur, mais celui d'un architecte qui contemple les fondations solides qu'il a posées, avant de pointer du doigt les chantiers de la souveraineté totale. Avec 20 millions de touristes, une industrie de pointe, une diplomatie diversifiée et un État social enfin déployé, le Maroc s'affirme non pas comme une puissance de domination, mais comme une puissance d'équilibre, de partenariat et de résilience. En citant pour conclure le verset « Dieu ne lèse pas les gens bienfaisants » , le Souverain rappelle que dans la gouvernance marocaine, la finalité ultime de la puissance n'est pas la gloire, mais le bien commun. Une éthique du pouvoir qui, à l'heure des nationalismes agressifs et des crises globales, donne au modèle marocain une résonance universelle. *Chercheur en Sciences politiques The post État stratège, Souveraineté et Nouveau contrat social : anatomie du discours du Trône 2026 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ghana’s second Independence moment: Why citizens must engage in constitutional reform
items.description: The 1992 Constitution of Ghana is the longest-lasting constitutional order since independence. For the 34 years during which the Constitution has been in force, it has fostered a rigid two-party political competition that has accommodated ethno-regional and religious cleavages, enabling a stable system of regular elections, largely peaceful turnover of governments, and peaceful coexistence. Unfortunately, it has not been enough to engender inclusive and sustained welfare benefits for the majority of Ghanaians, particularly the millions of unemployed youth, who feel despondent in the face of an uncertain future. Worse still, all signs indicate even further decline without a significant change of course. The ongoing process to reform the 1992 Constitution offers a pathway to recalibrate incentives, institutions and the general power arrangement to facilitate a sharper focus on political and socio-economic transformation that will enable life-changing and meaningful development. This is especially true if the process is undertaken with the seriousness, sincerity and credibility that is a prerequisite for a transformation project on a national scale. A credible and successful constitutional reform can only succeed if citizens seize this moment as an opportunity to free themselves from the oppression of highly polarized and transactional partisan politics that paralyzes leadership, processes and institutions for only one objective: the perpetuation of power for personal and group material gain, even to the detriment of the survival of the democratic order itself. Citizens must see this project as their second independence moment. Citizens are tired of the indignity of servitude to hyper partisan politics and processes A couple of weeks ago, heavy rainfall in Accra caused widespread chaos and loss of property and life across many communities. Emmanuel Ameyaw, writing in the Daily Graphic on May 29, 2026, on the perennial flooding in Accra, captures the dysfunctional system we have created and the causes of our problem. “ Dark clouds gather, heavy rain falls for a few hours, roads disappear under water, homes and shops are submerged, traffic grinds to a halt, and lives are lost. Politicians issue condolences, city authorities promise action, and then, somehow, we move on, until the next flood . But Accra’s flooding problem is no longer a natural disaster. It is a man-made crisis fueled by poor planning, greed, weak enforcement of regulations, and a dangerous disregard for nature and the environment.” In response to the devastating floods, the government called for a two-day national clean-up exercise. After the usual performative governance and physical exertions spiced with routine abuses of authority and brutality toward vulnerable citizens, the heaps of sand from the de-silted gutters remain on the roadside, days after the exercise, waiting to seep back into the very same drains from which they came. The reality is that this man-made crisis is fueled and nurtured by an anti-developmental, transactional, corrupt, state-weakening political system and culture that serves only a few elites and locks the rest of society in a perpetual survival mode. This political system and culture have placed politicians and political actors at the center of even the most basic functions of the State. In this ‘whom you know’ or ‘which politician you know’ State, parents supplicate their political contacts to secure access to schools for their wards, and citizens reach out to ‘big men’ and ‘big women’ to secure access to potable water or to fix roads for the community. Every day in the home or office of some Member of Parliament (MP), Minister or Mayor, people line up with all manner of financial demands to be presented for redress. Some have endured the indignity of travelling miles from villages and low-income communities across the country to solicit support for a health issue – a problem that a well-functioning healthcare system should fix. The MPs who are supposed to provide for all these needs are spending over $600,000 just to get elected and may have to ‘cough up’ a similar amount during their time in office to secure their political survival in the next electoral cycle. Some of the money used for campaigns and to respond to these demands is financed through manipulated public procurement, general corruption, and even proceeds from illicit activities like Galamsey . The problem of the dominance of money in politics has become so severe that even candidates for the position of Assembly Member in the supposedly non-partisan District Assembly are spending GHC 30,000 or more for campaigns. In 2020, CDD-Ghana estimated the cost of a competitive presidential political campaign at $100 million. This figure becomes even more alarming when one considers that most presidential aspirants would have attempted at least twice before becoming President. In essence, any politician who emerges from this monetized political system is under enormous pressure to ignore the pursuit of the public interest, fight corruption, or govern well. The window for self-correction is closing fast Our politics is creating paralysis and weakening state capacity and the ability to deliver basic services, but more importantly, to help the ordinary citizen fulfill their welfare goals. The paralysis is evident in more performative governance, the constant waste of public resources, the inability to plan long term, unaccountable governance and impunity, pervasive corruption, lack of meritocracy in the appointment of public officers, particularly to state enterprises, and ecocide. In the case of ecocide, the emblematic example is the devastation of Galamsey in our communities. The one problem that has allowed Galamsey to persist and now create one of Ghana’s biggest threats to law, order and public welfare is the involvement of partisan political actors and other elites. This perverse and deviant political logic, which favors the personal benefits of political actors and elites at the expense of millions of citizens and now threatens food and water security, reveals the deep hole that we have dug for ourselves. Unfortunately, there is no respite, and the headwinds are gathering. A number of incidents over the last year and a half are instructive. Sometime last year, the Ministry of Interior opened up recruitment into the security services. The ministry received over 500,000 applications when it was seeking to recruit 5,000. The President intervened to increase the number to 10,000, though it was clear that this was a financial burden the government had not planned for. A year before the Ministry of Interior recruitment exercise, the Ghana Armed Forces organized a recruitment exercise; thousands of young people trooped to the El Wak Stadium. The stampede that ensued killed six young women. The youth unemployment problem has persisted despite many government programs to address it. Meanwhile, we are graduating 400,000 high school students and 600,000 basic school students every year. The general sentiment among young people is that our current political arrangement is not working for them, and they are prepared to consider alternatives to the current governance arrangement and economic opportunities. Time to alter the political incentives for development as a starting point On January 26, 2026, the Constitutional Review Committee (CRC) established by President John Mahama submitted its full report to the President. The report titled “Transforming Ghana: From Electoral Democracy to Developmental Democracy” articulates a central reason for our checkered development. The only things going for us are regular, generally peaceful elections and stability, but neither has delivered the transformational and sustained development we crave. We have settled into a routine of changing governments with no discernible difference in development outcomes. To change course, our politics and governance must enable development: the delivery of a stable and productive economy. The CRC proposals offer a rearrangement of the rules to allow politics to support development. We need partisan politics because it creates a mechanism for resolving our differences, mobilizing common positions, and minimizing conflict if done right. As it is now, the way we do our politics impedes development. To change that, we must limit the dominance of the Executive Presidency in the management of the state. Digging a borehole in Bole should not require Presidential direction if there is effective local government. The State is there to produce and deliver high-quality public services like water, security, housing, healthcare, education, and social protection, to support the efficiency and productivity of the private sector, to create jobs and grow the economy, to build the infrastructure for the modern state and economy, and to deliver justice and fairness in interactions among citizens and between citizens and the state. Many of these tasks are technical and require people with the right competencies and experience to deliver them. This part of the state must be saved from partisan politics that distorts the primary missions of those institutions. Citizens must embrace the constitutional reform agenda as a personal project and take an interest in the government’s actions throughout the process. In the end, if democracy becomes entirely for sale to the highest bidder, citizens should abandon all hope of development and instead prepare for civil conflict similar to what has afflicted many countries on the continent whose democratic ideals and institutions have been eroded to the point of collapse.

items.title: Management has not abandoned Eastern Ports— Rivers Port manager
items.description: By Efe Onodjae The Manager of the Rivers Port Complex, Kenechi Okaeze, has assured stakeholders that the management of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has not abandoned the Eastern Ports, contrary to concerns expressed by some industry players. Okaeze gave the assurance while responding to questions from participants during an interactive session with members of the Maritime Correspondents Organisation of Nigeria (MARCON) in Port Harcourt where she represented the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, at the event. Responding to concerns that the Eastern Ports had been neglected, Okaeze said the Federal Government and the management of the NPA were making sustained efforts to rehabilitate and modernise port infrastructure across the region. “It is not correct to say that management has abandoned the Eastern Ports,” she said. “As we speak, some of the structures are being rehabilitated. Management has not ignored the Eastern Ports.” She disclosed that six berths at the Rivers Port Complex have already been reconstructed and strengthened as part of ongoing infrastructure renewal aimed at improving operational efficiency and accommodating larger vessels. According to her, the navigation channels are also being deepened to enable bigger ships to berth at the ports, thereby boosting cargo traffic and reducing the dependence on road transportation from ports in other parts of the country. “We know the Eastern Ports have proximity to key markets, which is why the government is making consistent efforts to ensure the ports are rehabilitated and fully functional. This will allow vessels to come directly here and save the cost of transporting goods by road,” she said. Okaeze noted that reviving the Eastern Ports would also address safety concerns associated with moving large volumes of cargo over long distances by road. She expressed optimism that the ongoing rehabilitation projects would soon yield results, assuring stakeholders that the Eastern Ports would regain their strategic position in Nigeria’s maritime sector. “I must assure you, don’t worry. Very soon, the Eastern Ports will start moving,” she said. The post Management has not abandoned Eastern Ports— Rivers Port manager appeared first on Vanguard News .
